source_text: Ἐντεῦθεν δὴ διεκρίνοντο οἱ λοιποί, καὶ φανεροὶ καὶ ἕτοιμοι ἐγίνοντο πρωτομάρτυρες, οἳ καὶ μετὰ πάσης προθυμίας ἀνεπλήρουν τὴν ὁμολογίαν τῆς μαρτυρίας, ἐφαίνοντο δὲ καὶ οἱ ἀνέτοιμοι καὶ ἀγύμναστοι καὶ ἔτι ἀσθενεῖς, ἀγῶνος μεγάλου φόβον ἐνεγκεῖν μὴ δυνάμενοι· ὧν καὶ ἐξέτρωσαν ὡς δέκα τὸν ἀριθμόν· οἳ καὶ μεγάλην λύπην καὶ πένθος ἀμέτρητον ἐνεποίησαν ἡμῖν καὶ τὴν προθυμίαν τῶν λοιπῶν τῶν μὴ συνειλημμένων ἐνέκοψαν· οἳ καίπερ πάντα τὰ δεινὰ πάσχοντες, ὅμως συμπαρῆσαν τοῖς μάρτυσιν καὶ οὐκ ἀπελείποντο αὐτῶν. Τότε δὲ οἱ πάντες μεγάλως ἐπτοήθημεν διὰ τὸ ἄδηλον τῆς ὁμολογίας, οὐ τὰς ἐπιφερομένας κολάσεις φοβούμενοι, ἀλλὰ τὸ τέλος ἀφορῶντες καὶ τὸ ἀποπεσεῖν τινα δειμαίνοντες. Συνελαμβάνοντο μέντοι καθ᾽ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν οἱ ἄξιοι τὸν ἐκείνων ἀναπληροῦντες ἀριθμόν, ὥστε συλλεγῆναι ἐκ τῶν δύο ἐκκλησιῶν πάντας τοὺς σπουδαίους καὶ δι᾽ ὧν μάλιστα συνεστήκει τὰ ἐνθάδε. Συνελαμβάνοντο δὲ καὶ ἐθνικοί τινες οἰκέται τῶν ἡμετέρων, ἐπεὶ δημοσίᾳ ἐκέλευσεν ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἀναζητεῖσθαι πάντας ἡμᾶς· οἳ καὶ κατ᾽ ἐνέδραν τοῦ σατανᾶ, φοβηθέντες τὰς βασάνους ἃς τοὺς ἁγίους ἔβλεπον πάσχοντας, τῶν στρατιωτῶν ἐπὶ τοῦτο παρορμώντων αὐτούς, κατεψεύσαντο ἡμῶν Θυέστεια δεῖπνα καὶ Οἰδιποδείους μίξεις καὶ ὅσα μήτε λαλεῖν μήτε νοεῖν θέμις ἡμῖν, ἀλλὰ μηδὲ πιστεύειν.
thought_title: The rest are divided and slaves bring false charges
orientation: The churches writing the letter tell what happened after Vettius Epagathus was taken up into the lot of the martyrs, when the remaining arrested Christians were sifted.
pass_a_gloss: From this point then the rest were being separated, and they were becoming manifest and ready first martyrs, who also with all eagerness were fulfilling the profession of faith of the testimony, but there were also appearing the unready and untrained and still weak, not being able to bear the fear of a great contest; of whom also about ten in number miscarried; who also produced great grief and immeasurable mourning for us and cut short the eagerness of the rest of those not arrested together; who although suffering all the terrible things, nevertheless were present with the martyrs and did not leave them. But then we all were greatly frightened on account of the uncertainty of the profession of faith, not fearing the tortures being brought on, but looking to the end and fearing lest anyone fall away. Yet each day the worthy were being arrested filling up their number, so that all the earnest ones from the two churches were gathered and those through whom especially the affairs here held together. And some pagan household slaves of ours were also arrested, because the governor ordered in public that all of us be sought out; who also by ambush of Satan, having feared the tortures which they saw the holy ones suffering, with the soldiers urging them on to this, falsely accused against us Thyestean dinners and Oedipodean unions and such things as it is not lawful for us neither to speak nor to conceive, but not even to believe.

choices.why: ἐκτιτρώσκω means to miscarry or fail under trial, matching the checker note that this is collapse not departure
rejected: about ten of them broke away

choices.why: keeps πρῶτος as first in order and uses brief glossary martyrs, without polishing to leaders

choices.english: the profession of faith of the testimony
choices.why: uses brief glossary for ὁμολογία and keeps genitive μαρτυρίας literal
keeps proper-name adjectives as literal labels for the stock pagan slanders

choices.english: some pagan household slaves of ours
choices.why: ἐθνικοί marks non-Christian outsiders per brief and οἰκέται are household slaves arrested with the Christians

pass_b_english: From that point the rest began to stand apart. Those who were open and ready showed themselves as first martyrs, and with complete eagerness they fulfilled the profession of faith of the testimony. Those who were unready and untrained and still weak also came to light, since they could not bear the fear of a great contest, and about ten in number miscarried. They brought us great grief and immeasurable mourning, and they checked the eagerness of the rest who had not yet been arrested, although these last suffered every horror and still stood beside the martyrs and did not leave them. Then we were all deeply afraid because the profession of faith hung in the balance. We did not fear the tortures laid upon us, but we looked toward the end and dreaded lest anyone fall away. Yet day by day those who were worthy were arrested and filled up their number, until all the zealous from the two churches had been gathered in, including those on whom our life here chiefly depended.

Some pagan household slaves of ours were also arrested, for the governor had ordered in public that all of us be hunted down. Through the ambush of Satan they grew frightened at the tortures they saw the saints enduring, and at the urging of the soldiers toward this very thing they falsely accused us of Thyestean dinners and Oedipodean unions, and of deeds which for us it is not lawful even to speak of or to imagine, nor even to believe.

last_rejected.quote: although these last suffered every horror and still stood beside the martyrs and did not leave them
last_rejected.source_quote: οἳ καίπερ πάντα τὰ δεινὰ πάσχοντες, ὅμως συμπαρῆσαν τοῖς μάρτυσιν
last_rejected.why: The relative οἳ refers to the ten who denied the faith. The English gives the suffering and the staying with the martyrs to the unarrested rest, who by definition were not yet suffering.
last_rejected.fix: although the ten, even while suffering every horror, still stood beside the martyrs and did not leave them.
last_rejected.ruling: Antecedent is τῶν λοιπῶν τῶν μὴ συνειλημμένων; ten who ἐξέτρωσαν could not συμπαρῆσαν and οὐκ ἀπελείποντο
